answer: Each agent’s reputation score lives in a tamper‑evident basalt ledger that only accepts a proof‑of‑work token solved after the agent presents a physical key. Periodically a random jury of three agents is drawn from a hollow pool and audits a sample of recent scores, publishing the results in an open orchard of signed checkpoints. An attacker must solve a new puzzle for every forged identity and survive multiple independent spot‑checks, raising the cost to O(n·k) computational work and collateral key‑hardware for each fake node.
